description: Return the setup for a "jig", the tool you build to make the real thing precisely. Use kind "tune-in-place" (default) when you are about to hard-code taste-based values in UI you are building: animation duration/easing/springs/stagger, particles, canvas physics, blur/glow/grain, gradient stops, shadow recipes, parallax speeds. It returns a control panel to wire to those parameters so the USER tunes by eye. Use kind "variant-canvas" when the user should choose between versions of one piece of UI before one is built: it returns a picker that shows three versions differing on one axis on the real screen, never ranked, for React, React Native, SwiftUI, Shopify or plain HTML. Use kind "standalone-tool" when the user wants a reusable custom tool instead: a generator, an image effect, a shader playground. That returns the Toolcraft starter kit (MIT). Before you say a screen is done, use kind "break" to render one component under hostile content (long text, no data, narrow containers) and report what visibly broke, kind "states" to build a page that shows every state it can reach (loading, error, empty, roles, plans) with a switcher, and kind "before-after" to prove a change with matching renders of the same screen. On this server the jig and the picker have a Send button: after you hand one over, call this tool with kind "wait-for-send" to receive what the person chose, then write it into the code.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

framework.description: The platform the jig or picker goes into. 'react' (default) for React/Next web projects; 'vanilla' for plain DOM or canvas work; 'react-native' for RN/Expo apps; 'swiftui' for SwiftUI apps; 'shopify' for Liquid themes. Only used when kind is 'tune-in-place' or 'variant-canvas'.

kind.description: What the user needs. 'tune-in-place' (default): a control panel for parameters in the UI you are building. 'standalone-tool': a separate reusable design tool, scaffolded with Toolcraft. 'variant-canvas': three versions of one piece of UI on the real screen behind a picker. 'wait-for-send': wait for the person to select Send on a jig or picker you handed over, and receive what they chose. 'break': render one component under every scenario that can reach it and report what visibly broke. 'states': a page with every state of one component and a switcher. 'before-after': renders of the same screen before and after your change.

title: Get a Jig for Parameter Work
